items.name: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten
items.duration: One or two years, as proposed by the artist
items.funding: Funded residency: a private studio, access to specialist technical workshops, an annual working budget (€2,500/yr) and a living stipend, funded via the Rijksakademie Artists Endowment Fund and Stichting Ammodo. The stipend is set per cycle and was €19,800 for the current intake — check the live open call for the figure that applies.
items.disciplines: All visual-art disciplines; multidisciplinary and research-led practices welcomed
items.summary: A long-horizon development residency organised around sustained studio practice and in-house technical support rather than exhibition output. Residents work alongside peers and a rotating programme of visiting art professionals.
items.applicationNote: One open call a year, opening on 1 January and closing at the start of February, for an intake beginning the following year; selection is judged in stages. Applicants are expected to have completed art training and to have several years of independent practice behind them.

items.name: Cité internationale des arts — "2–12" programme
items.duration: Two to twelve months, set by the artist's project
items.funding: Self-funded: the artist pays a monthly charge for the space. Provisionally from about €635/month for a live-in studio (25–50 m², furnished, with workspace) and roughly €265–680/month for a work-only studio (16–45 m²), varying with size. Rates are confirmed on selection and may change between editions. Many residents arrive instead via a partner funder that pays these costs.
items.disciplines: Open to all disciplines — visual arts, music, writing, performance, film, curating and research
items.summary: A large multi-studio complex in the Marais hosting residents across every discipline at once, rather than a small curated cohort. Selection weighs the reason the project needs to happen in Paris.
items.applicationNote: The self-funded "2–12" strand runs a recurring open call with an online application form. Partner-funded routes (including Institut français and other national and private funders) run separate calls on their own timetables.

items.name: Delfina Foundation
items.funding: Supported through partner organisations and funders rather than by open self-funding. Provision typically covers accommodation and work space in the Foundation's building, with living costs and production support set by the individual partner agreement; some calls expect the artist to secure a national funder that pays Delfina directly. Terms vary by call.
items.disciplines: Visual arts, curating, writing and research, usually gathered around a thematic programme
items.summary: London's largest host of international residencies, organised into thematic programmes. The Politics of Food, launched in winter 2014, is the best known and has involved over 100 UK and international practitioners. Residents live and work together in adjoining townhouses near Buckingham Palace, so the programme trades studio scale for proximity and conversation.
items.applicationNote: There is no single annual deadline. Several calls are posted a year, generally tied to a thematic programme or to a specific partner country or funder, so track both Delfina's open-calls page and the relevant national arts funder.

items.name: Künstlerhaus Bethanien — International Studio Programme
items.funding: Funded by external bursaries and partner institutions rather than by Bethanien itself. Support covers monthly living costs, studio rent, material support and a presentation in the on-site gallery; a stipend of around €1,500/month is commonly cited by partner funders. The house runs 25 studios.
items.summary: A year in a large private Berlin studio with curatorial support and a presentation at the end, which makes it one of the more career-consequential European residencies. The structural catch is that the place is brokered through a funder in your own country.
items.applicationNote: Applications can only be submitted through Künstlerhaus Bethanien's associated partner organisations, each running its own guidelines and timetable — partners are based in Australia, Belgium, Canada (including Quebec), Cyprus, Denmark, Korea, the Netherlands, Norway, New Zealand, Portugal, Singapore and Sweden. Unsolicited direct applications are not accepted.

items.name: Cove Park
items.duration: Short residencies of roughly two weeks to three months, negotiated with the artist
items.funding: Two tracks: Awarded Residencies, which are funded and normally include an artist fee and support costs, and Open Residencies, which are self-funded by the artist or their own grant. Confirm current terms directly.
items.disciplines: All art forms, the creative industries and researchers; individuals and collaborative groups
items.summary: A rural residency centre on a hillside site above Loch Long in Argyll, within reach of Glasgow, with residents accommodated in separate units and left largely to work alone.
items.applicationNote: Awarded Residencies are advertised through periodic open calls, often attached to a named fund or partner, so timing shifts year to year. Open (self-funded) Residencies are applied for separately.

items.name: MacDowell
items.funding: Fully funded with no residency fee: exclusive use of a studio, accommodation and meals. Need-based travel assistance and stipends are available to those who qualify; artists pay for their own materials.
items.disciplines: Architecture, film/video, interdisciplinary arts, literature, music composition, theatre and visual arts
items.summary: The oldest artist residency in the United States, founded in 1907 on a wooded campus near Mount Monadnock, awarding roughly 300 fellowships a year. Studios are scattered through the forest and lunch is delivered to the door — the design is for uninterrupted solitary working time.
items.applicationNote: Applications are reviewed in recurring cycles through the year covering different residency seasons, assessed anonymously by panels of discipline professionals on a work sample and project description.

items.name: Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture
items.funding: Tuition-based but heavily subsidised, with substantial scholarship support available to accepted participants; housing, food and studio space are included. Tuition and aid terms have changed between cycles — check the current year's published figures rather than relying on past ones.
items.disciplines: All disciplines; aimed at emerging artists
items.summary: An intensive nine-week summer programme for around 65 artists living as a community on a rural Maine campus, founded by artists in 1946. Resident and visiting faculty run studio visits, workshops and reading groups.
items.applicationNote: One annual open call, with decisions announced in the spring for that summer's session. Financial aid is handled alongside admission rather than after it.

items.name: Headlands Center for the Arts
items.funding: Sponsored: studio space, housing, prepared meals, and travel and living expenses. Confirm the current award terms and the number of places on the programme page.
items.disciplines: Artists across disciplines, local through international
items.summary: Housed in former military buildings inside the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, minutes from San Francisco but surrounded by coastal parkland. Selection weighs readiness to engage with the park setting and surrounding community, not past work alone.
items.applicationNote: An annual open call for residencies a year or more ahead, assessed by an independent jury panel. Check current eligibility rules before applying.

items.name: Fogo Island Arts
items.duration: Roughly four weeks for the open-call strand; longer for funded and partner residencies
items.funding: Depends on the strand. Funded and invited residencies cover travel, housing, studio, meals and a materials stipend. The open-call strand carries a participation fee and provides private accommodation and studio access — confirm the current fee and inclusions before applying.
items.disciplines: Professional contemporary artists, curators and writers across disciplines
items.summary: A remote North Atlantic island residency with architect-designed coastal studios, run by the Shorefast social enterprise. Residents typically give a public presentation or workshop, tying the programme into island life.
items.applicationNote: The open-call strand has its own annual application window. Funded and partner residencies are advertised as separate calls through the year.

items.name: Fundación Casa Wabi
items.duration: Sessions of roughly five to six weeks, with a small group in residence at once
items.funding: No residency fee: accommodation on site, studio space, communal meals and support for the required community project. Artists cover their own international travel. Confirm what else is included for the specific call.
items.disciplines: Open across disciplines; every proposal must include a community project
items.summary: A Tadao Ando-designed compound on the Oaxacan Pacific coast, founded by the artist Bosco Sodi. What distinguishes it is obligation rather than seclusion — residents must deliver a reciprocal project with a neighbouring community.
items.applicationNote: Places are filled through open calls and partnerships that vary between years, including a periodic open-call residency prize run with an external partner. Proposals are judged on the work and on the strength of the proposed community project.

items.name: Instituto Sacatar
items.duration: Multi-week fellowship sessions, typically around two months
items.funding: Funded fellowship: accommodation, meals, studio space and logistical support, with a small application fee. Artists pay their own airfare to Salvador and cover their own materials and incidental costs.
items.summary: Founded in 2001 on Itaparica island in the Bay of All Saints, Sacatar places residents inside Afro-Brazilian Bahia rather than adjacent to it.
items.applicationNote: An annual open call covering several sessions across the year, submitted through an online application platform with a modest application fee. Open to artists of any nationality and discipline.

items.name: Khoj International Artists' Association
items.duration: Several weeks, varying by programme strand
items.funding: Supported: travel to Delhi, a per diem, a production budget, studio space on the Khoj campus and shared accommodation. Terms vary by edition.
items.disciplines: Visual arts and interdisciplinary practice; editions are often framed by a research theme
items.summary: An artist-run organisation in Khirkee Extension that has anchored experimental practice in South Asia since the late 1990s, closing residencies with open studios rather than a finished exhibition. Peers is a separate long-running strand for emerging India-based artists.
items.applicationNote: Calls are issued per programme edition rather than on one fixed annual date, advertised some months ahead of the residency period. Peers runs as its own call for emerging artists based in India.

items.name: Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS) — Residency Programme
items.duration: Around three months for the creator strand; shorter for the curator strand
items.funding: Funded: living space, airfare, a daily living allowance and a project or research fee, plus studio space. Amounts are published per call and differ between the creator and curator tracks.
items.disciplines: Visual arts, design and architecture; a separate track for curators
items.summary: A residency run by Tokyo Arts and Space, a programme of the Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture, which gives residents institutional access to the city that independent programmes rarely provide. It suits research-driven projects that need Tokyo as subject or material.
items.applicationNote: An annual open call for the following year's programme, with separate application tracks for creators and for curators.

items.name: Sharjah Art Foundation Residency Programme
items.funding: Funded: travel to Sharjah, accommodation and a stipend, plus access to the Foundation's resources and networks. Confirm the current terms in the live call.
items.disciplines: Visual and performance artists, writers, researchers, musicians, filmmakers and other interdisciplinary practitioners
items.summary: Residents work between restored heritage buildings in Sharjah City and the Kalba Ice Factory, a former ice factory on the Gulf of Oman coast converted by the Foundation into an arts space. The programme is heavily oversubscribed.
items.applicationNote: An annual open call, open to local, regional and international applicants. Expect very high competition; the Foundation also runs a separate studio programme offering longer studio use.

items.name: NIROX Foundation
items.duration: Typically several weeks, negotiated case by case
items.funding: Partially funded: board and lodging, studio space and access to the foundation's network. Artists generally cover their own transport, materials and production costs. Confirm current terms directly with the foundation.
items.disciplines: Contemporary visual artists working across media
items.summary: Set in a private reserve inside the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site outside Johannesburg, alongside NIROX's sculpture park. Programming around each residency is negotiated individually with the artist.
items.applicationNote: There is no single fixed annual call. Some places are filled by invitation and others through partner-institution calls; direct proposals are also considered. Confirm the current route with the foundation before applying.

items.name: 32° East | Ugandan Arts Trust
items.duration: Around three months for the supported residency; longer, flexible periods for the self-funded strand
items.funding: Two routes. The supported residency provides accommodation, a studio, a materials budget and a stipend. A self-funded strand lets practitioners rent studio space at the centre. Confirm current amounts and availability.
items.disciplines: Visual artists; the self-funded strand also invites researchers, architects and curators
items.summary: An independent home for contemporary visual art in Uganda, which has built its own purpose-designed art centre in Kampala.
items.applicationNote: The supported residency is filled through a themed open call, typically annual. The self-funded strand has its own separate application route.

items.name: Bundanon
items.city: Illaroo, near Nowra, New South Wales
items.funding: No residency fee. A private studio matched to the practice plus on-site accommodation are provided; artists meet their own travel, food, materials and day-to-day costs.
items.disciplines: Visual and performing arts, literature, dance and music, plus environmental and scientific research
items.summary: Set on Arthur and Yvonne Boyd's gifted Shoalhaven River property, one of the largest artist residency programmes in Australia. Studios are purpose-specific — dance, music and workshop spaces among them — which is unusual at this scale.
items.applicationNote: An annual open call for the following year's programme, open to individuals, collaborative groups and organisations, and to emerging through established practitioners. Applicants nominate their preferred residency length and studio type.

items.name: McCahon House — Parehuia Residency
items.duration: Three months, with several residencies offered each year
items.funding: Funded: use of a furnished, architecturally designed house and studio plus a stipend, supported by public and private funders. Confirm current amounts in the live call.
items.disciplines: Visual arts, pitched at mid-career artists
items.summary: A purpose-built house and studio in French Bay, beside the cottage where Colin McCahon lived and painted in the 1950s, on the bush edge of west Auckland. The programme deliberately targets mid-career artists, a stage most residencies underserve.
items.applicationNote: An annual open call assessed by a selection panel. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens or permanent residents and able to live and work full-time at Parehuia for the term.
